taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: 1 phase had the tools designed for them

finalText:
I read RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html) and took each status code's reason phrase and section number from its own subsection of Section 15. I found no newer HTTP Semantics RFC in my search, so I treated RFC 9110 as the current specification.

**Cacheability.** Section 15.1 of the spec lists the codes defined as heuristically cacheable: "200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, and 501". It adds that all other status codes are not heuristically cacheable. Of your twelve codes, 203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414 and 501 are cacheable. Each of those sections also says "A NNN response is heuristically cacheable" in its own text. Codes 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422 are not on the list.

**Reason phrases.** Two differ from what older RFCs used: 413 is now "Content Too Large" and 422 is "Unprocessable Content".

**Quotes.** Where a quote runs across a line break in the RFC's plain-text layout, I joined it with single spaces. The sentence itself is unchanged.
